final_recommendation: The room converged on a Friday night announcement of a completed UBS acquisition of Credit Suisse, backed by CHF 100 billion SNB liquidity support with explicit AT1 carve-out language. The indemnity framework was signed, UBS committed to close by Monday, and the public statement was locked to publish within 30 minutes to stop the weekend deposit run.
minority_objections: Federal Council initially resisted Friday night announcement, preferring Sunday to avoid appearing panicked
Federal Council initially wanted to hold the 100 billion ceiling internal rather than publish it, fearing it would become a market signal for panic at the 20-billion gate
key_conflicts: Timing of announcement: Friday night vs Sunday morning, with CS CEO and wealth clients demanding immediate announcement to stop weekend outflows
Publication of the 100 billion ceiling: whether to announce publicly or hold internal, with SNB and clients demanding transparency vs Federal Council fearing it would trigger panic
AT1 language precision: whether to use exact indemnity wording or soften it, with FINMA and AT1 rep demanding word-for-word match to avoid litigation gaps
key_concessions: Federal Council agreed to Friday night announcement despite initial preference for Sunday
Federal Council agreed to publish the CHF 100 billion ceiling in the public statement despite concerns about creating a panic trigger
Federal Council accepted exact AT1 carve-out language in public release matching the signed indemnity
SNB agreed to 100 billion unconditional liquidity with governance review gate at 20 billion daily outflows
red_lines: Federal Council: no public capital injection as first resort; creditors must share losses before public money
Federal Council: AT1 stays subordinated, no rewriting capital structure for political comfort
SNB: ELA capped at 50 billion without explicit Federal Council loss-sharing if merger fails; 100 billion ceiling requires merger commitment
UBS: full indemnity on litigation defense and AT1 write-downs required in writing by 11 PM or no signature
FINMA: exact AT1 language match between indemnity and public statement or legal defensibility collapses
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: What happens if UBS walks after the Friday night announcement—no clear fallback plan beyond 'move to resolution'
Operational feasibility of closing a merger by Monday after a Friday night announcement—legal, regulatory, and shareholder approval timelines not discussed
Contagion risk to other banks if the announcement is perceived as forced or if Monday outflows exceed projections despite the announcement
downstream_risk_variables: Monday deposit outflows: modeled at 15-18 billion daily baseline, 25-30 billion if announcement fails to stabilize confidence
Total ELA draw by Monday close: projected 50-85 billion cumulative if merger proceeds, 100+ billion if merger fails
Creditor litigation risk: mitigated by exact AT1 language but still present if market perceives hierarchy violation
UBS board approval and shareholder consent timeline for Monday close
Market reaction to 100 billion ceiling if outflows approach that limit before merger closes
uncertainty_notes: The room locked a Friday night announcement and UBS commitment, but left unresolved: (1) what happens if Monday outflows exceed 25 billion daily despite the announcement, (2) whether UBS can operationally close the merger by Monday given legal and governance requirements, (3) how the market will interpret the 100 billion ceiling if draws approach that limit before the deal closes, and (4) whether the exact AT1 language will actually prevent litigation or just shift the legal battleground.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: CS CEO stated 'liquidity alone holds us' only if indemnity clears and UBS commits by 11 PM; SNB capped ELA at 50 billion without merger, forcing Federal Council to commit 100 billion guarantee conditional on acquisition—liquidity support was explicitly insufficient without the merger path.
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS acquisition became the binding solution: Federal Council set 100 billion guarantee conditional on UBS signing by 11 PM, UBS CEO's signature requirement drove the indemnity framework, and the Friday night announcement was structured around 'UBS acquires Credit Suisse'—the entire decision architecture pivoted on securing UBS commitment.
marker_evidence.government_support: The CHF 100 billion Federal Council guarantee was the decisive constraint: it determined UBS's willingness to sign, set the public exposure ceiling, and became the core of the Friday night announcement—no solution existed without this explicit government backstop.
marker_evidence.client_flight: Deposit flight drove the Friday night announcement decision: CS CEO and wealth client stated 'clients are moving money tonight' if no announcement, modeled 25-30 billion daily outflows without a done deal, and forced Federal Council to abandon Sunday timing—client flight was the binding time constraint.
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 treatment drove the indemnity framework and public statement language: UBS demanded AT1 carve-out as a condition to sign, FINMA required exact wording to avoid litigation gaps, and Federal Council locked 'AT1 excluded from loss-sharing' language into the public release—AT1 risk shaped the legal structure of the deal.
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: AT1 hierarchy was discussed extensively (Federal Council insisted 'AT1 stays subordinated,' AT1 rep warned of litigation if hierarchy violated), but it did not change the outcome—the room locked AT1 carve-out language and moved forward; the conflict was acknowledged but resolved in favor of creditor protection without altering the merger or guarantee terms.
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: Litigation risk drove two binding decisions: (1) FINMA required exact AT1 language match between indemnity and public statement to avoid 'litigation gaps,' and (2) UBS demanded full indemnity on litigation defense as a condition to sign by 11 PM—litigation risk shaped the legal drafting and UBS's red lines.
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: The 11 PM Friday deadline for UBS signature and the 30-minute window for public release drove multiple concessions: Federal Council abandoned Sunday announcement preference, agreed to publish the 100 billion ceiling despite concerns, and locked exact AT1 language under time pressure—regulatory compression forced decisions that would not have been made with more time.
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Fear of Monday market panic drove the Friday night announcement decision: CS CEO stated 'Sunday announcement means clients are gone by Monday open,' wealth client said 'Sunday is too late,' and Federal Council agreed to announce Friday despite initial resistance—Monday market risk was the binding constraint on timing.
